---
title: "Is the mean or median a better summary of a numeric variable?"
---

## The question

Is the mean or median a better summary of a numeric variable?

## What to check and do

1. Identify the observations and measurement units. 2. Calculate mean and median. 3. Inspect the distribution for skew or clusters before choosing a 'typical' value.

## Worked example: faithful

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("faithful")
answer <- ru_apply("mean_median", data=d, x="waiting")
stopifnot(answer["mean"]>0,answer["median"]>0)
```

The mean and median summarize waiting time between geyser eruptions. Because the data have distinct clusters, neither number tells the entire story; inspect a histogram too.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("mean_median", data=your_data, x="numeric_column")
```

If there are large outliers, compare median and mean rather than removing observations automatically.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("mean_median")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
